assign.now: found four real disagreements with the earlier audit: stream-with-block, assistant-stream, padding-audit are each only PARTLY what the owner asked for; writing verify.jsonl and the page next

log.msg: devbar-chat, devbar-path-bar, verbatim-echo, full-log, devbar-questions, message-on-page, log-voice, keep-the-log-fresh: agree with the earlier audit, each re-checked independently (live curl to /ai-logs/, live eval of the open dev bar, exact-string match of an owner card against the known verbatim chat log, a direct read of the mastermind skill file).

DISAGREE stream-with-block: the chat-stream-deaf bug really was fixed (Tail.js/live.js url-normalize), but the owner's actual ask -- 'Block should stop reloads only' -- is still false today. Socket.js:159 `changed()` returns before it ever reaches the CSS-restyle branch (Socket.js:167) when window.$BLOCKRELOAD is set, so Block still freezes live CSS swaps too. The same defect was already named in research.jsonl (id dk8x9, 2026-08-18) and never fixed. Verdict: partly, not done.

DISAGREE assistant-stream: the chunk-by-chunk streaming code is real (Server/plugins/Assistant.js start/chunk/flush/finish) and was proven -- but only on a private scratch server (port 8142) against a SCRATCH board.jsonl, per that task's own task.jsonl. The REAL board.jsonl has zero chunk lines, ever (grep -c '"chunk"' = 0), and all 54 real assistant cards carry hand-picked ids like 'assistant-tiers', never the 'a-HHMMSS' id Assistant.start() mints -- meaning every reply the owner has actually read arrived as one whole finished card via the manual say.mjs relay, not as a live-typing reply. Verdict: differs, not done.

DISAGREE padding-audit: .card and --pad-card are real, in framework.css (line 285, 438, 471), and two lint checks landed in Server/health.mjs -- but the implementing task's own landing line says outright 'nothing on the live site wears .card yet.' Checked the exact card that started the complaint: dev/DevBar/devbar.css:295-298's .dev-says-card uses padding: var(--pad), not --pad-card and not the .card class -- confirmed live (eval on the open dev bar): computed padding 12.8px, class list has no 'card'. The visible 3px bug is fixed, but through a second, parallel token, not the 'one token for all cards' the owner asked for. Verdict: partly, not done.

assign.outcome:
**8 of the 11 dev-bar requests hold up; 3 that were graded `done` are not quite.** Checked every row against live code and the running site, never against the earlier audit's own word.

The three disagreements, biggest first:
- **`assistant-stream` (was done -> differs).** The reply-types-itself-out mechanism is real, but was proven only on a private scratch server against a scratch file. The real board.jsonl has zero streamed replies, ever -- every real answer the owner has read is one whole hand-posted card.
- **`padding-audit` (was done -> partly).** The `.card` style is real and well designed, but its own builder says outright "nothing on the live site wears `.card` yet." The exact cards that started the complaint still use the old, different padding rule.
- **`stream-with-block` (was done -> partly).** The reported bug is genuinely fixed. But Block still also freezes CSS live-updates, not just reloads -- `Socket.js` line 159 -- contradicting the owner's own "Block should stop reloads only," a defect already named in this repo's own research log over a month ago.

The other 8 (devbar-chat, devbar-path-bar, verbatim-echo, full-log, devbar-questions, message-on-page, log-voice, keep-the-log-fresh) were each independently re-checked -- live curl to `/ai-logs/`, a live headless open of the dev bar, an exact-string match of a logged owner card against the known verbatim record -- and hold up.
